channel.title: The Grant Desk - Cross-disciplinary & Social Impact, next 30 days
channel.description: Paid open calls, fellowships and residencies in AI, tech, research, and digital and mixed-media arts, sorted into the right pile. Updated as new calls land on the desk. Filtered to: Cross-disciplinary & Social Impact, next 30 days.

item.title: Red Quincho: Beca Constelaciones 2026 (4th Edition)
item.description:
Organisation: Red Quincho

Location: Rotating urban and rural Red Quincho spaces across Argentina; residency runs September to December 2026.

Award: ARS 1,000,000 (around USD 690) per grant toward mobility, living costs and production, plus one month of lodging. 15 grants available. No application fee.

Duration: One-month residency split into two 15-day placements at different spaces.

Deadline: 09 Aug 2026

Beca Constelaciones is Red Quincho's mobility and production grant for artists, curators and researchers doing territory-based work, now in its fourth edition. Each recipient spends one month in residence, split into two 15-day placements at different member spaces across Argentina, pairing an urban and a rural context. The grant covers mobility, living costs and production, with lodging provided. Backed by Fundacion Williams, CCEBA and Fundacion Santander through the CABA Mecenazgo scheme. ELIGIBILITY IS RESTRICTED: of the 15 grants, 13 are for people resident in Argentina and 2 are for people currently living in Spain. Artists, curators and researchers apply through separate forms; Spanish-based candidates face an additional jury evaluation. Deadline 9 August 2026 at 23:59 Argentina time.

Open call details

item.title: Digital Cultures Festival 2026: Best of Poland Open Call
item.description:
Organisation: Digital Cultures Festival (Monster Mind Studio); Pitch Award funded by the Adam Mickiewicz Institute

Location: Warsaw, Poland (live pitches on 24 September 2026)

Award: Best of Poland Pitch Award: a career development grant of up to PLN 5,000 (funded by the Adam Mickiewicz Institute) for the jury's top pick, to support participation in a European industry event. Up to 10 creators also receive pitch coaching and expert feedback. No application fee.

Duration: Live 7-minute pitch showcase on 24 September 2026

Deadline: 01 Aug 2026

Best of Poland is the Digital Cultures Festival's showcase for work at the intersection of art and technology. Open to anyone working creatively in digital media (artists, filmmakers, game developers, UX designers, programmers, curators, students and more) with projects that show how technology fosters genuine human connection and addresses contemporary social change. Eligible formats include VR, AR, interactive film, games, net art and cross-media works; both completed and in-progress projects qualify. Selected creators present 7-minute live pitches on 24 September 2026 in Warsaw; the jury's top pick receives the Best of Poland Pitch Award, a career development grant of up to PLN 5,000 funded by the Adam Mickiewicz Institute to support participation in a European industry event, and up to 10 creators receive pitch coaching with festival director Anna Szylar and expert feedback. Free to apply via the form on the festival site. Deadline: 1 August 2026.

Open call details

item.title: MOVIDA: Labs on Dance and Technology 2026/27
item.description:
Organisation: MOVIDA (Movement and Virtual Intelligence for the Development and Accessibility of Artists and Audiences)

Location: Four labs across Europe: Bucharest (Romania), Dusseldorf (Germany), Lisbon and Montemor-o-Novo (Portugal), and Tallinn (Estonia). Applications are accepted only from duos of one dancer and one creative technologist; you cannot apply solo. Both members must reside in an EU or Creative Europe eligible country, so Netherlands-based applicants qualify.

Award: EUR 1,200 gross per artist (EUR 2,400 per duo), plus travel and accommodation covered, plus a production budget of up to EUR 500 per duo. Accessibility and personal-assistance costs are covered by separate agreement. No application fee.

Duration: Nine days per lab, scheduled between 3 December 2026 and 11 February 2027

Deadline: 03 Aug 2026

MOVIDA is a Creative Europe co-funded consortium pairing academic institutions with dance centres across four European cities. Sixteen duos, each made up of one dancer and one creative technologist, are selected across four themed labs: AI and accessibility in Bucharest, AI and AR/VR in Dusseldorf, AI and robotics in Lisbon, and AI and mental health in Tallinn. Applicants are assessed on demonstrated capability in integrating technology with live performance, computational creativity, and audience interaction. Participants selected for the labs receive fast-track consideration for the MOVIDA residencies running in 2027 and 2028.

Open call details

item.title: Association Francoise pour l'oeuvre contemporaine x Cite internationale des arts: Research and Creation Residency 2027
item.description:
Organisation: Association Francoise pour l'oeuvre contemporaine / Cite internationale des arts

Location: Paris, France (Marais site of the Cite internationale des arts). Open to artist-authors of any nationality and any discipline, mid-career or established, with no age limit. Applicants must be comfortable working in French or English. Note: the studio-apartments do not meet current accessibility standards for people with disabilities.

Award: Grant of EUR 1,000 net of tax per month, plus a furnished studio-apartment (20 to 35 sq m, combining living and working space), international return travel to Paris airports or stations, travel insurance, and capped research support against receipts. Additional fees apply for accompanying persons. No application fee.

Duration: Approximately 12 weeks, 5 January to 26 March 2027

Deadline: 16 Aug 2026

Launched in 2025, this research and creation residency explores the links between contemporary art, psychiatry and the human sciences. It is expressly not a therapeutic programme. It seeks artists whose practice resonates with the notion of the clinical, meaning a situated approach that works closely with lived narratives and specific contexts, and that engages with questions of care. The selected artist receives tailored support from Albertine de Galbert, a clinical psychologist and exhibition curator, including four to six working sessions, alongside networking and meeting time with programme partners. Outputs include an ongoing online journal, a mid-residency open studio, and a closing presentation (exhibition, public talk or publication) defined with the artist. Applications go by email as a single PDF of no more than 15 MB to residence@francoiseartmemo.fr, and require a two-page CV, a ten-page portfolio, a two-page statement of intent, and a letter of recommendation from an institution or a curator. A jury of four to six art and psychiatry specialists decides, with results announced in September 2026.

Open call details

item.title: FUJIFILM GFX Challenge Grant Program 2026
item.description:
Organisation: FUJIFILM

Location: Open to residents of the countries/regions listed under Entry Submission on the program page. Final content showcased on fujifilm-x.com plus planned exhibitions in various countries.

Award: 5 Global Grant Awards of USD 10,000 and 10 Regional Grant Awards of USD 5,000. All recipients also get complimentary use of a GFX System camera body (including the FUJIFILM GFX ETERNA 55 filmmaking camera) and two GF lenses for the duration of the project, plus mentoring and technical assistance from Fujifilm technicians and product experts. Total approximate retail value of all awards: USD 229,500. No purchase necessary; no entry fee.

Duration: Application window 16 June to 17 August 2026. Production period concludes in May 2027, after which final content is showcased on fujifilm-x.com and in a planned series of exhibitions.

Deadline: 17 Aug 2026

The GFX Challenge Grant Program, sponsored by FUJIFILM and running since 2021, awards 5 Global Grant Awards (USD 10,000) and 10 Regional Grant Awards (USD 5,000) to help aspiring creatives bring imaging projects to life. It is designed to nurture emerging and promising content creators, giving them the opportunity to create content on topics with significant meaning to them while gaining experience with FUJIFILM GFX System gear, including the GFX ETERNA 55 filmmaking camera. Proposed projects may be submitted as still photography or in movie format. AWARDS: both tiers include complimentary use of a GFX System camera body and two GF lenses for the duration of the project, plus mentoring and technical assistance from Fujifilm technicians and product experts. At the end of the production period in May 2027, recipients' final content is showcased on fujifilm-x.com, with a series of exhibitions planned in various countries. ELIGIBILITY: open to both amateur and professional photographers and videographers who are residents of the countries/regions listed in the Entry Submission section of the program page; not open to employees or officers of FUJIFILM and its subsidiaries. TO APPLY: combine three items into a single PDF: (1) the preformatted cover letter (downloadable from the program page); (2) the project proposal covering descriptive plan, objectives, evaluation and outcome measures, communications, how you will use the Fujifilm partnership and mentoring, schedule, and budget; (3) a portfolio for each individual involved. Proposals must be in English (optionally accompanied by a version in your own language; language proficiency is not judged). Entry period 16 June to 17 August 2026.

Open call details

item.title: Night as Commons and the Dark Side of Light: Residency (Transylvania)
item.description:

Award: EUR 30/day allowance, plus accommodation and travel (EUR 400 under 5,000 km; EUR 800 over), with green mobility, family, and accessibility top-ups. EU-funded. 6 weeks. No application fee.

Deadline: 01 Aug 2026

Hypha etc. hosts a six-week EU-funded residency (1 October to 10 November 2026) in Campu Cetatii, Transylvania, on the theme Night as Commons and the Dark Side of Light: night, darkness, and light pollution, a strong fit for media and installation practices. Support: EUR 30/day allowance, accommodation, travel allowance (EUR 400 under 5,000 km, EUR 800 over), plus green mobility, family, and accessibility top-ups. ELIGIBILITY: artists based in Creative Europe countries except Romania. Deadline 1 August 2026.

item.title: Connections Through Culture Grants 2026 (British Council)
item.description:
Organisation: British Council

Location: International collaboration grant. Each application must involve at least one UK-based partner and at least one partner based in an eligible participating country; each partner must be legally based in the country they apply from throughout the project.

Award: Grants of between GBP 5,000 and GBP 15,000. Free to apply.

Duration: Project-based; develop and deliver collaborative projects across a range of themes and art forms.

Deadline: 12 Aug 2026

Connections Through Culture (CTC) grants are designed to enable meaningful partnerships, cross-cultural exchange and long-term collaboration between the UK and participating countries. In 2026, CTC incorporates the grants programmes formerly known as Biennials Connect (Visual Arts) and Architecture, Design and Fashion Biennials and Festivals Grants, and serves as the British Council's major Arts grants programme for 2026 (in place of International Collaboration Grants). It offers grants of between GBP 5,000 and GBP 15,000 to support creative practitioners, cultural professionals, artists, organisations, festivals, biennials, hubs and collectives to develop and deliver collaborative projects across a wide range of themes and art forms, including applied arts, architecture, curating, dance, design, digital, drawing, education, fashion, film, installation, interdisciplinary work, painting, performance, photography, printmaking, public art, research, sculpture, social practice, sound art, textiles, video, visual arts and writing. ELIGIBILITY: applications must involve collaboration between at least one UK-based partner and at least one partner based in an eligible participating country; each partner must be legally based in the country they are applying from at the time of application and throughout the project activity period. PARTICIPATING COUNTRIES: Albania, Argentina, Australia, Bangladesh, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Colombia, Mainland China, Egypt, Indonesia, Kazakhstan, Kenya, Kosovo, Lebanon, Malaysia, Mexico, Montenegro, New Zealand, Nigeria, North Macedonia, Pakistan, Palestine, Peru, Philippines, Saudi Arabia, Serbia, South Africa, Tanzania, Thailand, Tunisia, Turkey, United Arab Emirates, UK, Ukraine, Uzbekistan, Venezuela, and Vietnam. Eligible applicants include artists and creative practitioners, arts and cultural organisations, festivals and biennials, cultural professionals, creative hubs/networks/collectives, and organisations working across arts, culture and the creative sectors. Note: applications involving projects organised by or taking place as part of Visual Arts, Architecture, Design, Fashion and Craft festivals should be made by the festival or biennial organisation rather than by individual artists, designers or practitioners. No application fee. Deadline 12 August 2026.

Open call details

item.title: Social Shifters Global Innovation Challenge 2026
item.description:
Organisation: Social Shifters

Location: Global; open to youth-led ventures from anywhere in the world.

Award: Multiple awards of up to USD 15,000 each (reported grants from USD 3,000 to USD 15,000), plus pitch coaching, a finalist showcase, free founder support from registration, and ongoing access to fellowships and paid work through the Shifters 100 alumni network that corporate partners recruit from. Free to enter.

Duration: Submissions close 31 August 2026; finalists announced October, winners December 2026

Deadline: 31 Aug 2026

Social Shifters, a Scottish-registered charity backed by corporate partners, runs its Global Innovation Challenge as a funnel into a longer founder-development pipeline rather than a one-off prize. ELIGIBILITY: founders aged 18 to 30 at submission, leading a fully youth-led venture that is already live and producing measurable social or environmental impact, aligned to at least one Sustainable Development Goal; concept-stage ideas and student projects do not qualify. Multiple winners receive up to USD 15,000 each, plus pitch coaching, a finalist showcase, and ongoing access to fellowships and paid work through the Shifters 100 alumni network. Free coaching is available from the moment you register, so the payoff to registering early is high. Submissions close 31 August 2026 (5pm UTC), with finalists announced in October and winners in December 2026. Apply at https://www.socialshifters.co/global-innovation-challenge/.

Open call details

item.title: Stimuleringsfonds + Film Fund: Immerse\Interact 2026 (second round)
item.description:
Organisation: Stimuleringsfonds Creatieve Industrie and the Netherlands Film Fund

Location: Netherlands. Requires Dutch Chamber of Commerce (KvK) registration.

Award: Development: EUR 15,000 for individual makers (plus up to EUR 5,000 coaching, max EUR 20,000) or EUR 25,000 for producers (plus up to EUR 5,000 coaching). Realisation: up to EUR 35,000 for individual makers or up to EUR 125,000 for producers (Fund covers max 85 percent). No application fee.

Duration: Project-based, development and realisation phases.

Deadline: 25 Aug 2026

Immerse\Interact is a joint grant scheme of the Stimuleringsfonds Creatieve Industrie and the Netherlands Film Fund for immersive and interactive media projects (VR, MR, AR and other interactive storytelling). It supports artistic projects with a supporting cinematic component, in which fiction or non-fiction storytelling in relation to interactive (web-based/mobile) or immersive technologies (XR, room-scale projections) is central. It funds both development and realisation. Development support is EUR 15,000 for individual makers (plus up to EUR 5,000 coaching, capped at EUR 20,000 total) or EUR 25,000 for producers (plus up to EUR 5,000 coaching); the coaching contribution requires a motivation from both applicant and coach plus the coach's CV, and the development phase must result in a usable prototype. A maximum of six development contributions are awarded per round, to keep the development and realisation budgets in balance. Realisation support is up to EUR 35,000 for individual makers or up to EUR 125,000 for producers (the Fund covers a maximum of 85 percent of the production budget); note that at realisation stage the producer may not also be the director, screenwriter or designer. A separate Presentation Procedure offers presentation grants for projects previously supported by Immerse\Interact after 1 January 2022. EUR 600,000 is available per Fund in 2026. Open to professional makers, collectives and producers with a demonstrable track record in immersive or interactive media; applicants must be registered with the Dutch Chamber of Commerce (KvK). The second 2026 round runs 24 June to 25 August 2026 (opens 24 June 15:00, closes 25 August 16:00 CEST). No application fee. Questions: immerseinteract@stimuleringsfonds.nl.

Open call details

item.title: EU-Japan Fest: Mobility Support 2026 (15 August 2026 Cut-Off)
item.description:
Organisation: EU-Japan Fest Japan Committee (in partnership with Culture Next)

Location: Travel between Japan and European Capitals of Culture / Culture Next member cities

Award: JPY 50,000 to JPY 150,000 per applicant, depending on applicant and travel category. No application fee.

Duration: Travel period April 2026 - September 2026 (applications must be submitted at least 6 weeks prior to travel)

Deadline: 15 Aug 2026

The EU-Japan Fest Japan Committee supports individuals and organisations developing projects between Japan and European Capitals of Culture (past, present or future) as well as other Culture Next member cities. PURPOSE: support travel for research, project planning, and collaboration, building creative networks aimed at realising Japan-Europe arts and culture projects. THEMES (for Japan-Europe collaborative projects): Youth Empowerment; Nature & Green; Diversity (DEI); Social Regeneration. Projects may include participants from other regions (e.g. Asia) joining a Japan-Europe project. TARGET APPLICANTS: members of European Capital of Culture teams; artists and project organisers (including curators, designers, etc.); researchers in culture/arts; social entrepreneurs. TIMING: applications must be submitted at least 6 weeks prior to the travel date; this cut-off covers travel in April 2026 - September 2026. DEADLINE: this card is for the 15 August 2026 cut-off (other cut-offs each have their own card). APPLY via the Culture Next collaboration page.

item.title: Stimuleringsfonds: Open Call Fresh Perspectives 2026
item.description:
Organisation: Stimuleringsfonds Creatieve Industrie (Creative Industries Fund NL)

Location: Netherlands (Dutch fund; cross-sector collaboration)

Award: Two-phase grant. Phase 1: ten grants of EUR 10,000 (max 5 months, startup 1 December 2026 to 30 April 2027) to prepare, explore and prototype the project. Phase 2: ten grants of EUR 50,000 (max 12 months, implementation 1 September 2027 to 31 August 2028) for projects selected and fully completed in Phase 1. No application fee.

Duration: Phase 1 max 5 months; Phase 2 (if selected) max 12 months

Deadline: 25 Aug 2026

Open call from the Creative Industries Fund NL (Stimuleringsfonds) for cross-sector collaboration projects that offer new perspectives on current challenges such as climate, housing, polarisation, migration or inequality of opportunity. The procedure runs in two phases. In Phase 1, the applicant and partner use the period to prepare and kick off the project, further explore the theme, intended end product and collaboration, and investigate possibilities (including working on a prototype or proof of concept), concluding with a project plan, budget and collaboration agreement. Phase 2, open only to projects selected and fully completed in Phase 1, focuses on implementation and requires both a written application and a presentation to the advisory committee; projects may deliver various end products (an activity, intervention, event, publication, service, product or process) accompanied by a suitable form of knowledge sharing such as a presentation, symposium or publication. ELIGIBILITY: applicants working with at least one partner in cross-sector collaboration; see the fund's open-call page for full eligibility details. The Phase 1 application window runs from 19 May 2026, 15:00 CEST to 25 August 2026, 16:00 CEST.

Open call details
